dietEvidence.body: The skull and dentition indicate herbivory. No gut contents are known; the diet is inferred from anatomy.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: An early sauropodomorph known from hatchlings, juveniles and adults. The name refers to the tiny size of the first specimens, which were hatchlings.
summary: An early sauropodomorph known from hatchlings, juveniles and adults. The name refers to the tiny size of the first specimens, which were hatchlings.

discovery.body: Named by Bonaparte & Vince, 1979. The record is known from the Laguna Colorada Formation, Santa Cruz, Argentina. A growth series includes eggs, embryos, hatchlings, juveniles and adult material.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: A growth series including eggs, embryos, hatchlings and adult material.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Laguna Colorada Formation, Santa Cruz, Argentina. U–Pb CA-ID-TIMS zircon dates from tuffaceous siltstones in the bearing interval give 192.78 ± 0.14 and 192.74 ± 0.14 Ma, an Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) maximum age. The older Norian assignment was based on associated Dicroidium flora; the radiometric dates supersede it for this interval.

fossilEvidence.title: Nesting and herd assemblage
fossilEvidence.body: More than 100 eggs and remains of about 80 individuals, ranging from embryos to adults, were recovered from a restricted stratigraphic interval. Some skeletons are clustered by age class. The eggs and bones are directly preserved; colonial nesting and herd behaviour are interpretations of that assemblage.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: Hatchlings have proportionally large heads and short limbs; adults are robust with a moderately long neck. The growth series includes embryos, hatchlings, juveniles and adults.

anatomy.title: Body plan
anatomy.body: Hatchlings were quadrupedal and adults bipedal. The shift is inferred from digital models, limb proportions and the position of the centre of mass, not from trackways.

behaviour.body: Eggs and a bonebed of at least 80 individuals, from embryos to adults, show that Mussaurus nested and congregated in age-segregated groups. Pol et al. (2021) interpret this as colonial nesting and herd structure; the behaviour is inferred from the assemblage, not observed directly. Herbivory is inferred from skull and dental anatomy. General social, parental or migratory behaviour beyond this assemblage is not asserted.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a growth series including eggs, embryos, hatchlings and adult material. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The Laguna Colorada Formation is now dated by U–Pb CA-ID-TIMS zircon geochronology to about 192.8 Ma (Early Jurassic, Sinemurian), not the Late Triassic Norian age used in older sources. Adults reached roughly 6–8 m and 1.2–1.6 t; the first specimens were hatchlings about the size of a mouse, which explains the name. Adults are reconstructed as bipedal and hatchlings as quadrupedal. The 2021 bonebed supports colonial nesting and age-segregated grouping; those are inferences from the assemblage, not direct observations of behaviour. The 2021 study reports more than 100 eggs and 80 individuals; age segregation is an inference from clustering, not observed behaviour.
